  • The rural health clinic also has a full-time FNP and general surgeon, with a pediatrician position being recruited.

  • Nursery support is required; approximately 180 deliveries annually. A full-time pediatrician is being recruited to provide most newborn coverage.
  • New graduates and visa candidates are welcome.

A typical day is AM rounding in the hospital. Our EHR is Meditech in both the hospital and clinics. Most doctors have 4 or 5 patients to round on when the census is at its maximum of 25. We have been running a census of 10 lately. Rounding on average takes 45 minutes. When complete, the physician steps next door to the rural health clinic (RHC) where they can see an average of 25 patients. The RHC also has a full-time FNP, a general surgeon, and a pediatrician (when the position is filled). The medical attending also shares call responsibilities. One doctor will be on call at night for the entire medicine service at the hospital and will accept ER admissions and calls from the medical/surgical floor as needed. The rotation is currently 1:4. We plan to transition to a nocturnist model, where the attending will see their patients in the AM and the nocturnist will handle all ER admissions and medical/surgical issues at night.

job.title: Family Medicine PA – Los Angeles, CA | $140K–$160K; MAT & Mobile Health
job.description:
Seeking a bilingual Physician Assistant to join a community health team in Los Angeles, CA, providing primary care, Medication-Assisted Treatment and mobile health services.

Location: East Los Angeles, California
Salary: $140,000–$160,000 annually
Schedule: Full-time


A mission-driven, nonprofit community health organization in Los Angeles is seeking a bilingual Physician Assistant to join its interdisciplinary primary care team. This position offers the opportunity to provide meaningful, patient-centered care to culturally diverse and medically underserved communities across multiple outpatient locations and through a mobile health program.

The organization is a Federally Qualified Health Center offering integrated medical, pediatric, behavioral health, women’s health, dental, pharmacy and supportive community services. Its patient-centered approach emphasizes access, prevention, chronic disease management and addressing the medical and social factors that affect long-term health.

This is an excellent opportunity for a Physician Assistant who enjoys variety, community-based medicine and caring for patients across the lifespan. The incoming provider will serve as a float clinician throughout East Los Angeles and provide services through the organization’s Mobile Health Unit. Experience treating substance use disorders and providing Medication-Assisted Treatment is required.

  • Competitive annual salary of $140,000–$160,000 based on experience, skills and internal equity
  • Full-time, outpatient position
  • Provide primary and preventive care to pediatric and adult patients
  • Float between community health locations in East Los Angeles
  • Participate in a Mobile Health Unit serving patients throughout the community
  • Work alongside physicians, advanced practice providers, behavioral health professionals, community health workers and other support staff
  • Integrated care model with access to behavioral health, dental, women’s health, pharmacy and community resources
  • Care for a culturally and linguistically diverse patient population
  • Opportunity to make a direct impact within underserved Los Angeles communities

Responsibilities

  • Obtain and document comprehensive medical and social histories
  • Perform physical examinations and clinical assessments
  • Diagnose and manage acute and chronic medical conditions
  • Develop individualized, evidence-based treatment plans
  • Order and interpret laboratory testing, imaging and other diagnostic studies
  • Provide preventive care, health screenings, wellness education and counseling
  • Manage chronic conditions and support patients with long-term self-management
  • Provide care to patients across the lifespan, including pediatric and adult populations
  • Evaluate and treat patients with substance use disorders
  • Provide Medication-Assisted Treatment and ongoing SUD care management
  • Prescribe medications in accordance with applicable laws, regulations and clinical protocols
  • Collaborate with physicians and other members of the interdisciplinary healthcare team
  • Refer patients to specialty care, behavioral health, social services and community resources
  • Conduct pre-visit planning and review relevant laboratory, imaging, consultation and discharge records
  • Provide float coverage at outpatient clinics and through the Mobile Health Unit
  • Support culturally and linguistically appropriate patient education and communication
  • Participate in team huddles, case conferences, departmental meetings and care-management activities
  • Assist with quality-improvement initiatives, staff education, data collection and program evaluation
  • Provide appropriate oversight and guidance to medical assistants, community health workers and other assigned team members


Qualifications

  • Graduate of an accredited Physician Assistant program
  • Current California Physician Assistant license
  • Current certification as a Physician Assistant
  • Experience providing Medication-Assisted Treatment for substance use disorders
  • Experience assessing, treating and managing patients with substance use disorders
  • Pediatric care experience preferred
  • Bilingual fluency in English and Spanish required
  • Ability to provide compassionate care to culturally and socioeconomically diverse populations
  • Strong clinical judgment, communication and interdisciplinary collaboration skills
  • Comfortable traveling between outpatient locations and working in a mobile health setting
  • Valid California driver’s license
  • Reliable automobile and required automobile insurance coverage
  • Ability to successfully complete required background, physical and tuberculosis clearances

Additional Position Highlights

  • Street medicine experience is preferred.
  • California Physician Assistant licensure is required. Provide clinical care under a supervising physician and established written protocols, with clinical supervision from the Chief Medical Officer.

About the Community

East Los Angeles offers a community-centered setting with a rich Latino cultural heritage, neighborhood restaurants and local markets. Nearby Boyle Heights is home to Mariachi Plaza, the traditional marketplace El Mercadito, and Self Help Graphics & Art. Hollenbeck Park adds a neighborhood green space for time outdoors.

Living in the Los Angeles area places arts, live entertainment and cultural events within reach, while the Eastside offers its own distinct food, music and community traditions. This role provides a chance to build relationships across East Los Angeles neighborhoods through both clinic-based care and a Mobile Health Unit.

job.title: Bilingual FNP opening just north of Boston, MA - top community health clinic
job.description:
Bilingual Nurse Practitioner – Primary Care

Join a respected, mission-driven nonprofit healthcare organization serving a culturally diverse patient population throughout Massachusetts’ Merrimack Valley. For more than four decades, this community health system has provided comprehensive, high-quality care through a network of clinical locations and has earned national recognition for its work in community medicine.

The organization delivers family medicine, internal medicine, pediatric and geriatric care and sponsors an established Family Medicine Residency Program. This is an excellent opportunity for a bilingual Nurse Practitioner who values collaborative care, patient education and meaningful service to the community.


Responsibilities

  • Assess patients and obtain relevant medical, medication, allergy, psychosocial and family histories
  • Diagnose and manage acute illnesses, chronic conditions and episodic exacerbations
  • Review abnormal laboratory results and determine appropriate treatment or follow-up
  • Develop individualized care plans based on clinical findings and patient priorities
  • Provide clear, culturally sensitive education regarding wellness, illness, treatment and rehabilitation
  • Identify the need for additional services, patient education or specialty referrals
  • Collaborate with physicians, case managers, family-planning professionals and other members of the care team
  • Involve family members or significant others in the care plan when appropriate
  • Deliver care in accordance with approved clinical protocols and established standards of practice
  • Evaluate patients’ responses to treatment and adjust care plans as needed
  • Document education, treatment recommendations, patient understanding and follow-up needs
  • Serve as a clinical resource for healthcare team members
  • Participate in quality-improvement initiatives and support changes that improve patient care
  • Assist with the orientation and education of new employees or students when requested
  • Help develop and maintain patient and staff educational resources
  • Travel between nearby clinical locations as needed

Qualifications

  • Licensed or eligible for licensure as a Nurse Practitioner in Massachusetts
  • At least two years of recent Nurse Practitioner experience
  • Fluency in both Spanish and English required
  • Ability to work effectively within a multidisciplinary, team-based environment
  • Strong clinical assessment, communication and patient-education skills
  • Willingness to learn from and share knowledge with colleagues
  • Commitment to culturally responsive, community-based healthcare

Why Join?

  • Pay or shift range: $105,000 USD to $135,000 USD
  • Full benefits
  • Make a direct and lasting difference in an underserved community
  • Work within an established, mission-focused nonprofit organization
  • Join a collaborative, patient-centered healthcare team
  • Care for a culturally and clinically diverse patient population
  • Practice within an organization recognized for leadership in community medicine
  • Benefit from an educational environment connected with a Family Medicine Residency Program
  • Enjoy a role that is professionally challenging, flexible and deeply rewarding

The Community:

Located just 30 miles north of Boston, the city offers convenient access to the cultural, educational, and recreational amenities of Greater Boston, New Hampshire, and the New England coast. The Merrimack Valley combines urban diversity with easy access to mountains, beaches, and year-round outdoor recreation, making it an excellent place to build both a career and a life.

job.title: Invasive Cardiologist - North Atlanta, GA | $500K–$600K+ Potential | True Partnership Track | No Private Equity
job.description:
A growing, physician-owned cardiovascular practice in the North Atlanta metro is seeking a Board-Certified or Board-Eligible Invasive (Non-Interventional) Cardiologist to join its expanding team.

This is an excellent opportunity for a cardiologist who wants the clinical autonomy and long-term financial upside of private practice without the constraints of private equity or hospital employment. The group is in an active growth phase, expanding across several desirable North Atlanta communities and building for long-term physician ownership.


Opportunity Highlights

  • $425,000–$500,000 base salary, depending on experience
  • $500,000–$600,000+ total compensation potential
  • wRVU-based production incentives
  • Defined 2–3 year partnership track
  • Genuine equity ownership opportunity
  • No private equity
  • Physician-owned and physician-operated
  • Up to $15,000 relocation assistance
  • 401(k) with profit sharing
  • Comprehensive medical, dental and vision benefits
  • Malpractice coverage
  • $3,000 annual CME allowance plus 3 paid CME days
  • Opportunity to help shape the growth of an expanding multi-location practice


Practice Environment


Join an established cardiovascular practice serving one of the fastest-growing regions in the Southeast. The group combines the resources of a sophisticated cardiology organization with the autonomy and collegiality of private practice.


The practice is IAC-accredited in Nuclear Cardiology and Echocardiography and offers extensive in-office cardiovascular testing and diagnostics, including:

  • Nuclear cardiology
  • Echocardiography
  • Stress echocardiography
  • Vascular ultrasound
  • Holter and event monitoring
  • Pacemaker interrogation
  • Planned PET/CT cardiac imaging


Physicians also maintain privileges at several major hospitals throughout the North Atlanta region, providing access to strong hospital resources while preserving an independent practice model.


Position Details


The incoming physician will practice invasive, non-interventional cardiology in a combination of outpatient and hospital settings.


Responsibilities include:

  • Full-time outpatient cardiology
  • Hospital rounding
  • Invasive diagnostic procedures
  • Shared call coverage among the physician team
  • Practice across multiple North Atlanta locations
  • Collaboration with an experienced clinical and administrative team
  • Dedicated scheduling support
  • Opportunity for PA/NP support as the practice continues to grow


The group is seeking a cardiologist who wants more than an employed position and is interested in helping build and grow a physician-led organization.


A Real Partnership Opportunity


This is a genuine equity partnership track—not simply a productivity designation.


During the first several years, the incoming physician will receive competitive salary, benefits and mentorship while building a patient base and becoming integrated into the practice.


The anticipated path includes:

  • Years 1–2: Associate physician with salary, benefits and productivity opportunity
  • Years 2–3: Transparent equity buy-in process with terms discussed in advance
  • After partnership: Profit sharing, governance participation and ownership in the growing practice


Partners have a meaningful voice in clinical direction, scheduling, staffing and strategic growth.


The practice plans to continue adding cardiologists as it expands throughout North Atlanta, giving the incoming physician an opportunity to help shape both the future team and the direction of the organization.

Live and Practice in the North Atlanta Metro

North Atlanta offers an especially attractive combination of excellent schools, family-friendly communities, outdoor recreation and convenient access to a major metropolitan area.

The practice serves rapidly growing communities throughout the northern Atlanta suburbs, an area known for strong demographics, continued residential development and a highly insured patient population.

Residents enjoy:

  • Highly regarded public school districts
  • Safe, desirable suburban communities
  • Convenient access to Atlanta's dining, entertainment, professional sports and cultural attractions
  • Easy access to Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport
  • Lake recreation and boating
  • Hiking and outdoor activities throughout the North Georgia mountains
  • Mild climate with four seasons
  • Lower overall cost of living than many comparable major metropolitan markets


This is an outstanding opportunity for an Invasive Cardiologist seeking strong compensation, clinical autonomy, true ownership potential and the ability to build a long-term career in one of the Southeast's fastest-growing markets.

job.title: Primary Care Internist opening in Wichita Falls, TX - $450K+ potential comp, 10-14 patients per day
job.description:
Seeking BE/BC Internal Medicine physician to join hospital-employed team in Wichita Falls, Texas. Here, Internal Medicine is practiced the way it should be: with longitudinal relationships, protected physician time, and strong system resources that allow you to focus on complex adult care without burning out.

  • Average of 10-14 patients per day
  • 4.5-day work week
  • Epic EMR
  • Schedule Autonomy - you decide how your schedule is built and your volume
  • Strong support to reduce clerical burden and keep you practicing medicine
    (APP's, RN nurse navigators, community health workers, social workers, experienced practice managers)
  • A transition clinic that streamlines post-discharge care allowing you to build longitudinal management of complex patients instead of urgent follow-ups.


Hospital is a technologically advanced, independent, not-for-profit Level II Trauma Center ranked among the top 2% of hospitals in Texas.


Compensation & Benefits:

  • Guaranteed base salary floor of $250k plus wRVU production incentive
  • Total compensation potential of $450k +
  • PSLF-eligible employer
  • Sign-on bonus & relocation assistance
  • CME allowance & residency stipend
  • Marketing & practice development support
  • NO STATE INCOME TAX

This is a wonderful community to have a great work-life balance.

Your children enjoy great public schools or you may opt to send them to one of several, excellent private schools. Your family is so close to Dallas/Fort Worth that you can drive in for dinner, shopping or to catch a Cowboys game, but you feel insulated from the crime, traffic and the “Big City” hassles. In your downtime, you and your family relax on the lake, at your ranch or taking a bike ride on our 24 mile trail.

  • Exceptionally low cost of living
  • 10-minute average commute
  • Physician-friendly community
  • Easy access to Dallas/Fort Worth and Oklahoma City for flights, entertainment, and weekend escapes
  • Live your way: golf course neighborhoods, ranch properties, upscale developments, or serene established communities
  • Highly regarded public and private schools for outstanding educational options
  • An active lifestyle scene with a 24-mile trail system, lakes, parks, and year-round outdoor recreation
  • Rich cultural scene: symphony orchestra, ballet, opera, theater, museums, and the arts

job.title: Family Medicine Opening in the Black Hills of SD — Clinic, Hospital & ED in One Role
job.description:
A well-established, community-based healthcare organization in the Black Hills region of South Dakota is seeking a BE/BC Family Medicine physician to join a robust, full-spectrum practice.


Position Highlights:

  • Full-time Family Medicine role with true full-spectrum practice across clinic, hospital, ED, and long-term care
  • 1:7 call rotation covering inpatient and emergency department responsibilities
  • Cradle-to-grave care for patients across all ages and acuity levels
  • One integrated 42,000 sq. ft. facility with clinic, 12-bed hospital, and 24/7 ED under one roof
  • Strong, established primary care team with excellent clinical support
  • On-site diagnostics for fast, efficient patient care
  • Nursing home care responsibilities within a local long-term care facility
  • Broad-scope practice with autonomy and continuity across all settings


Compensation & Benefits:

  • Highly competitive base salary
  • Starting and retention bonuses
  • Relocation assistance
  • Paid malpractice coverage
  • CME reimbursement
  • Comprehensive physician benefits package (health, retirement, and additional coverage options)
  • Marketing and practice growth support


Location & Lifestyle:

Living in this part of the southern Black Hills offers a rare blend of rugged natural beauty and small-town living surrounded by some of the most iconic landscapes in the country. Residents enjoy immediate access to vast outdoor recreation, including hiking, biking, fishing, camping, and wildlife viewing, with national and state parks, granite peaks, lakes, and scenic byways just minutes away. Despite its peaceful, close-knit community atmosphere, the area is within a few hours’ drive of larger regional hubs such as Rapid City, Sioux Falls, and even Denver for expanded dining, shopping, travel, and cultural opportunities. With strong schools, a safe environment, and a lifestyle deeply connected to nature and outdoor adventure, it offers an appealing balance of professional focus and everyday quality of life.

Step immediately into a fully developed busy practice with immediate referral sources. Become a part of a data informed practice where there is full visibility of all the processes related to running an efficient and successful practice. We offer a competitive salary with a full complement of benefits including paid time off, CME and moving allowances.

  • Fastest growing Metroplex, economically diverse city with high median family income
  • Popular state for practicing physicians: favorable tort system, low cost of living, no state income tax, and temperate climate.

Practice Info:

Our patients have access to joint injections, physical therapy, biological treatments, orthopedic surgery and everything in between. We have a collaborative team of board-certified and double-board-certified orthopedic specialists who practice alongside sports medicine specialists, physical therapists, interventional spine specialists, chiropractors and highly skilled physicians’ assistants.

job.title: Certified Nurse Midwife - Dallas, TX - full scope care, collaborative care model
job.description:
Seeking full-time CNMs excited to join a dynamic and growing practice of OB/GYNS and CNMs in the thriving community of Dallas-Fort Worth, TX.

Work in a collaborative care model with Physicians, Midwives, dietary needs, wellness coaches, holistic care, that allows providers to work at top of their skills. Clinic model is at least 1 FTE OBGYN at a director level, 3.5 Laborists, and 4 CNMs.

You will:

  • Take first call
  • Independently manage and provide full-scope midwifery care in our outpatient clinic including comprehensive obstetric and gynecological services
  • Collaborate with clinical colleagues (including OB/GYNs; RNs; LCSWs, health coaches, lactation counselors, childbirth educators and other specialists)
  • Provide day-to-day expertise and leadership on Labor & Delivery, including in-house clinical coverage
  • Triage and care for emergent obstetric patients, working collaboratively with RNs and OB/GYNs
  • Provide first assist surgical support
  • Participate in quality improvement initiatives
  • Attend skills training and drills for high acuity/low frequency events


Qualifications:

  • Experience in managing intrapartum, postpartum, and OB triage in a hospital setting (2 yrs experience preferred)
  • Ability to work effectively as part of a collaborative OB/CNM practice
  • Strong communication skills and intrapersonal skills
  • Value patient preferences/choice, shared decision making, and a holistic care approach
  • Neonatal Resuscitation Program (NRP) certification and Basic Life Support (BLS) certification by start date
  • Active certification with AMCB
  • Current RN and APRN license in TX
  • Additional certifications in Obstetric Ultrasound, Advanced Fetal Monitoring, and/or Lactation consultation are preferred


Benefits

  • Competitive compensation
  • Health; dental & vision, with an HSA/FSA option
  • 401(k) with employer match
  • Paid time off
  • Paid parental leave
  • Payment for professional liability coverage, license renewals, including DEA
  • Professional development budget
  • Leadership training and advancement opportunities, if desired


About the Company:

Group is a network of modern women's health practices working in partnership with hospitals to reimagine the maternity and women's healthcare experience. We are restructuring the traditional approach to care to create an experience that is good for patients and good for providers. We do that by combining a tech-enabled, wellness-focused care program that women love with a clinical system that helps us drive continuous quality improvement and ensure work-life balance for our care team. We work with clients across all life stages to empower and support them to live happier, healthier, more fulfilling lives. With strong collaborative care teams; passionate administrators and a significant investment in operational support, providers are well-supported to bring their very best to the work they love.

We know that it is our teams that make us special, and we are committed to creating a supportive work environment. Our teams are rigorous and data-driven and drawn together by a relentless commitment to improving outcomes. We value real talk, accountability, empathy, and humor. You will be joining a collaborative environment dedicated to providing excellent patient care & committed to ensuring providers have work-life balance.


The Community:

Located in the heart of North Texas, the Dallas area offers the energy of a major city with endless opportunities for both work and life outside of the office. Residents enjoy a strong economy, diverse neighborhoods, nationally recognized dining, and access to professional sports, arts, and entertainment year-round. The region is known for excellent transportation access, including one of the busiest international airports in the country, making travel simple and convenient. Outdoor enthusiasts can take advantage of parks, trails, and nearby lakes, while families appreciate a wide variety of schools and activities. With no state income tax and a relatively affordable cost of living compared to many other large U.S. metros, the area continues to attract professionals from across the country. Whether seeking urban amenities, suburban comfort, or career growth, this area offers an outstanding place to live and work.

job.title: Psychiatry PA-C opening near Florence, SC with Award-Winning Practice
job.description:
Seeking Psychiatric Nurse Practitioner or Physician Assistant to comprehensive psychiatric care, including assessment, diagnosis, and treatment of patients with mental health disorders. Works collaboratively with physicians, therapists, and other health professionals to deliver integrated behavioral healthcare. Provider functions in accordance with his/her collaborative practice agreement signed by the collaborating physician as required by the South Carolina Nurse Practice Act/South Carolina Board of Medical Examiners. Responsibilities include

  • Conduct psychiatric evaluations and mental status examinations.
  • Diagnose and manage mental health conditions such as depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder, and schizophrenia.
  • In collaboration with the primary care provider, develop individualized treatment plans, including prescribing and monitoring psychotropic medications.
  • Provide crisis intervention and ongoing psychotherapy as appropriate.
  • Complete timely documentation in the EMR for each patient encounter and review patient medical records for accuracy and completeness, ensuring timely medical record documentation.
  • Requests, obtains, and evaluates results of screening tests.
  • Monitors the treatment regimen in selected populations.
  • Demonstrates proficiency in all the above. Assessed by medical and clinical preceptors through record audits and one-on-one training and observation, at least once a year, or if needed.
  • Confer with collaborating physician when needed for consultation, information, etc.
  • Conduct quality assurance review utilizing clinical measures by life cycle.
  • Perform duties and support practice transformation as a Patient Centered Medical Home
  • Serve as an advocate for the center and serve as liaison to local hospitals and health organizations as appropriate.


Education and Experience

  • Master’s or Doctoral degree in Nursing or a master’s degree in physician assistant sciences from an accredited program.
  • Must be licensed to practice as an Advanced Practice Nurse (APRN) or as a Physician Assistant in the state of South Carolina
  • Certified by a nationally recognized nursing organization that certifies nurse practitioners practicing in an extended role or, if a physician assistant, certified by the National Commission on Certification of Physician Assistants (NCCPA)
  • Certification as a Psychiatric-Mental Health Nurse Practitioner (PMHNP-BC) is preferred, or if a physician assistant Certificate of Added Qualifications (CAQ) in Psychiatry from the NCCPA is preferred
  • A minimum of two years’ experience functioning as a psychiatric nurse practitioner or a psychiatric physician assistant is strongly preferred
  • BLS certification is required

Location


This position will work at several locations. Location assignment will be prioritized by the volume of patients requiring the care. Two days per week will be in Hartsville, SC.


Hours

Monday - Friday; 8:00 AM - 5:00 PM

*** $10,000 Sign-On Bonus ***

Are you a compassionate, non-invasive cardiologist seeking a dynamic environment where clinical excellence, innovation, and community intersect? Who We Are Looking For

We are seeking board-certified or board-eligible non-invasive cardiologists for either traditional (outpatient/inpatient) or hospitalist (inpatient-only) roles. Why Join Medical Group at Medical Center

Founded in 1904, Medical Center has long been a trusted healthcare pillar for northern Indiana, northwestern Ohio, and southeastern Michigan. Some clinics also have Lead MAs and Case Managers, with plans for expansion of Case Manager support.
  • Technology & Efficiency:
  • Utilizes Epic EMR with comprehensive training and ongoing support from Onsite Support Assistants (OSAs).
  • DeepScribe is used in almost every clinic for note-taking to streamline administrative tasks.
  • Seamless communication ensures every admission and ER visit is sent to the PCP via Epic, keeping you informed of patient care transitions.
  • Procedures and Virtual Appointments: All practices perform minor procedures based on provider preference , and all clinics have the capability for virtual appointments.
  • Patient-Centered Medical Homes: Many practice sites are designated patient-centered medical homes, some with CPC+ status.

  • Productivity & Incentive Bonuses:
  • Opportunity for additional compensation if calculated wRVU Compensation exceeds the base compensation at fiscal year end (July-June).

  • Paid Time Off: 37 days of paid vacation, approved in advance by Director.

Community and the Great Lakes Bay Region

Home to over 500,000 happy residents, the communities of the Great Lakes Bay Region are growing cities filled with freshwater adventures and natural wonders, beckoning you to Lake Huron’s Saginaw Bay and beyond. Saginaw, Midland, Bay City, and Mount Pleasant represent the heart of the Region. From the bustle of Downtown Saginaw to the quiet agricultural communities of Gratiot County, the Great Lakes Bay Region spans diverse communities throughout the heart of Michigan. Thanks to its blue collar heritage, convenient access to the rest of the world and a well-educated population, businesses of all types are finding that this tremendous area of the country is their perfect home.

Have fun! Go sailing under the stars, take a Michigan ecotour, unwind on a wine tasting river cruise, or set out for one of the best walleye fisheries you’ll find on a guided Michigan fishing charter. When warmer weather sweeps in, so do seemingly endless days filled with the best stuff summertime in Pure Michigan has to offer. Lounging riverside listening to live music, watching one of the Midwest's largest fireworks displays on the Bay City riverfront, or seeing epic tall ships from around the globe sail into port...just scratches the surface of what you can experience here. When temps dip and snow falls, Michigan transforms into a winter playground. All season long, our cold-weather activities will entice you to get out and enjoy the white stuff. It won’t take long to see why the Great Lakes State loves winter. Find the perfect winter resort that caters to your favorite winter activity.

job.description:
Full service orthopedic practice that has been serving Houston, TX for almost 40 years is seeking Physical Therapist to join its team. This is an 11 physician, independently-owned multispecialty group with 3 offices located in Northwest Houston.

  • New grads welcome
  • Schedule varies - flexibility! Clinic is open 7-6 Monday-Friday, we offer Part time, PRN or full time (flexible schedule)

Step immediately into a fully developed busy practice with immediate referral sources. We offer a competitive salary with a full complement of benefits.

  • Fastest growing Metroplex, economically diverse city with high median family income
  • Popular state for practicing physicians: favorable tort system, low cost of living, no state income tax, and temperate climate.
  • Practice payor-Mix is: 51% private insurance; 36% Medicare (and Medicare replacement); 3% Self-pay; 5% Workers comp; 5% other
  • Built-in referral base with Orthopaedic surgeons, Non-surgical specialists, Pain management physician and Rheumatologist
  • Practice possesses a full range of ancillary services including but not limited to diagnostics, physical therapy and DME.


Practice Info:

Our patients have access to joint injections, physical therapy, biological treatments, orthopedic surgery and everything in between. We have a collaborative team of board-certified and double-board-certified orthopedic specialists who practice alongside sports medicine specialists, physical therapists, interventional spine specialists, chiropractors and highly skilled physicians’ assistants.

Our locations are equipped with today’s most advanced diagnostic and therapeutic technologies, including an electromyography system and digital radiography machines to make taking and processing images simpler, faster, more accurate and more convenient. Additionally, we are able to produce custom-molded thermoplastic upper extremity orthoses and provide various other types of durable medical equipment. Other advanced orthopedic treatments offered at our centers include personalized knee replacements, ultrasound-guided corticosteroid and hyaluronan injections, concussion management, bone marrow aspirate concentrate (BMAC) treatments and minimally invasive/arthroscopic surgery.

Clinic is seeking to add a Family Medicine PA to their team. Be a part of a healthcare movement as you grow your career. The size and culture of the organization provides an opportunity to work closely with leadership, lead initiatives, and see the results of your hard work. The only limitations to your ability to be impactful are your passion and creativity.

The organization's service area covers 3,687 square miles. This area includes not only all of Adams County but the northern third of Franklin County and the southern third of Grand County as well. The group is aware of and engaged with the specific challenges these patient populations face, especially when they reside in remote, rural areas where there is a shortage of health professionals. Position Highlights

  • Busy practice w/ trained support staff.
  • 21-24 patients per day on a 7 hr clinical day
  • Clinic Hours are Monday-Friday, 8 am to 5:30 pm
  • Clinic also has a psychiatry services on site.
  • Provide primary, acute and chronic care, including emergency care, in order to achieve, maintain and restore optimal patient outcomes.
  • Engage in health assessment, diagnosis, and treatment of frequently occurring types of illnesses and other medical problems.

We came together, joined in a common purpose to provide health care to all.

Also known as the “heart of WA wine country,” the Tri-Cities is a rapidly growing mid-sized metropolitan area with more than 200 wineries within an hour’s drive. Seeking an Advanced Practitioner to join our team specializing in Heart Failure care. As a leading provider of cardiology services, we are committed to delivering compassionate, high-quality care to our patients. This is an excellent opportunity for a motivated individual to work alongside experienced cardiologists and healthcare professionals in a collaborative, patient-centered environment.

As an Advanced Practitioner in Heart Failure, you will play a key role in the management and care of patients with complex heart failure. You will work closely with the cardiology team to assess, diagnose, and develop comprehensive treatment plans for patients, ensuring optimal outcomes. This role requires a compassionate and knowledgeable individual who is passionate about heart failure management and improving patient quality of life.

  • Perform comprehensive patient assessments and diagnostic evaluations related to heart failure.
  • Develop and implement individualized care plans, including pharmacologic and non-pharmacologic interventions.
  • Monitor patient progress, adjust treatment plans as needed, and provide ongoing education to patients and families.
  • Collaborate with cardiologists, nurses, and other healthcare professionals to provide coordinated care.
  • Order and interpret diagnostic tests, including echocardiograms, EKGs, and lab work.
  • Participate in patient rounds, case discussions, and follow-up care.
  • Provide patient education regarding heart failure management, lifestyle modifications, and medication adherence.
  • Stay current with the latest research and advancements in heart failure care.
  • Document all patient interactions and maintain accurate and up-to-date medical records.

Requirements:

  • Current certification as a Nurse Practitioner (NP) or Physician Assistant (PA).
  • Previous experience in cardiology or heart failure management preferred.
  • Strong clinical knowledge and the ability to manage complex cardiac conditions.
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to work well within a multidisciplinary team.
  • Compassionate, patient-focused attitude with a commitment to providing high-quality care.

Compensation:

  • Competitive salary and benefits package: $130,891-$150,933
  • $5,000 starting bonus.
  • $5,000 retention bonus.
  • Opportunity for professional development and continuing education.
  • Collaborative and supportive work environment.
  • Health, dental, and vision insurance options.
  • 403 b Retirement savings plan and paid time off

Community Info:

Discover an excellent work/life balance in NY’s Capital District- a medium sized area offering all the amenities of a larger urban area in a beautiful, scenic, and affordable setting. A stable economic setting; we have a strong and expanding presence in healthcare of every type, in higher education, and enjoy a unique position as the capital of the Empire State. The Capital District includes the cities of Albany, Schenectady, and Troy- and the surrounding area includes Clifton Park and Saratoga Springs. The region has excellent year-round outdoor recreation available, including excellent golf, water-sports of all kinds, camping, hiking, and great skiing. It offers a wealth of cultural offerings and activities, including several renowned museums (the Albany Institute of History and Art, The NY State Museum), theaters (Proctor’s, The Palace) fine dining, and a year-round events calendar full with music and sporting events (The Times Union Center & Saratoga Performing Arts Center.) Excellent public and private schools are available, as are affordable homes and reasonable taxes. Higher education opportunities abound in our region with nearly 30 colleges and universities in the region and we are part of NY’s Tech Valley.

job.title: CRNA/Nurse Anesthetist Opening in northeast Maine
job.description:
Medical Center currently has a need for a full-time CRNA to join 5 full-time CRNA’s and two anesthesiologists staffing our five Operating Rooms. The OR performs an average of 250 cases per month, including approximately 15 births per month. Hours are typically 7:00 a.m. – 3:00 p.m. Practice with flexibility and autonomy under a medical supervision model, enjoying a manageable call schedule (1 in 4–5) with minimal trauma. Our Surgery percentages generally average 50% general surgeries, including eyes and urology; 25% Orthopedics; 10% OB/GYN; and 15% other surgeries. Head/heart cases are not performed.

Our Anesthesia department employs a Medical Supervision model which allows great flexibility and autonomy for our CRNA’s.

Our CRNA’s are employees of the hospital and are offered a highly competitive annual salary plus an additional call pay stipend. We offer 10 weeks of vacation, relocation assistance, forgivable educational loan assistance, and continuing education assistance.


Opportunity requirements:

  • BLS and ACLS Certified with AANA Certification
  • Maine Licensure
  • Skill requirements include General, Spinal, Obstetrical, Pediatric and Thoracic Anesthesia except open heart; Bier Block, Ventilation Management in the OR, (establishing and maintaining an airway; various modes of ventilation); and arterial line.
  • Epidural and peripheral nerve block expertise.
  • Central line placement.

CRNA’s are employees of the hospital and are offered a highly competitive annual salary – which is negotiable based on experience, plus an additional call pay stipend. job.description:

Our clinical staff is fully engaged in quality improvement, earning multiple blue ribbons from the Maine Health Alliance. We are a designated preferred provider for State of Maine employees, and have been recognized by Anthem Blue Cross / Blue Shield as a preferred provider based on the demonstrated quality of care provided to our patients.

For over 38 years the system has provided care to a service area population numbering about 35,000 people. Its has a dedicated, volunteer Board of Directors and a strong, supportive relationship with the Medical Center. It has received recognition as a Patient-Centered Medical Home (PCMH). PCMH is a comprehensive, coordinated team-based approach that enables patients to take an active role in their health status and decision making. This innovative model puts patients at the center of care as their primary care practitioner leads an interdisciplinary team of health care professionals to treat all aspects of the patient’s health. NCQA Patient-Centered Medical Home Recognition raises the bar in defining high-quality care by emphasizing access, health information technology, and coordinated care focused on patients.

The Community:

A recent list from Backgroundchecks.org that compiles the ten safest places in Missouri concludes that St. Louis County — and specifically, west county — is leading the state. Easy access to St. Louis City, one of America’s most historic cities. The city’s past, as a staging post for westward expansion, as an industrial and transportation hub, and as one of the country’s musical and baseball capitals, is etched into the city’s DNA. The city is undergoing regeneration that is bringing new jobs and research facilities, revitalizing abandoned industrial land and attracting tourists. Known as the “Gateway to the West,” St. Louis can be described as a big city with small-town charm. Whether you’re looking to be in the heart of downtown or settle in the suburbs, you’ll easily be able to find the perfect neighborhood for you and your family.

If you’re looking for fun things to do in St. Louis with the family, you won’t have to look far. The Community:

Welcome to the Land of Enchantment. Nestled in the heart of the enchanting high desert of New Mexico, Santa Fe stands as a city uniquely intertwined with history, culture, and natural beauty. Renowned for its distinctive adobe architecture, vibrant arts scene, and a spiritual ambiance, living in Santa Fe is an experience marked by a tapestry of positives.

From the breathtaking landscapes of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains to the thriving arts community, the city draws residents seeking a blend of tranquility and creativity. With stunning views and Rio Grande trail rides, the region boasts sacred Native American sites such as Tent Rocks, Lake Abiquiu, Ghost Ranch, Bandelier, Bisti Badlands, White Sands, Taos Gorge, and Chaco Canyon. Santa Fe offers many outdoor options for the recreational enthusiast including skiing, biking, hiking, fishing, and frisbee golf. With over 200 restaurants in town, the dining options are endless. It is a city of diverse and vibrant neighborhoods, each contributing to the city’s unique charm.

Situated at 7500 ft, the high desert climate is characterized by four distinct seasons. The city is renowned for its abundance of sunny days, averaging over 300 days of sunshine annually. The mild, high desert climate provides warm summers and crisp winters, making outdoor activities enjoyable year-round. The pleasant spring and fall seasons offer a perfect balance, with comfortable temperatures that invite residents and visitors alike to explore the city’s scenic landscapes, outdoor festivals, and cultural events.

This is a full-time inpatient pediatrician role, focusing on providing care to newborns and pediatric patients admitted to the hospital. The provider will manage a range of inpatient responsibilities, primarily related to newborn care with some pediatric admissions. The role is critical to maintaining comprehensive care for pediatric patients in a hospital setting.

SCHEDULE:

  • 8 hours in-house per day (8:30 AM - 4:30 PM)
  • 7 on/ 7 off schedule
  • 24/7 coverage with 16 hours of on-call responsibilities
  • Typical census: 8-15 newborns per day and 0-2 pediatric patients per day
  • Call responsibilities include: Nurse phone consultations, potential admissions from the ED, and attending high-risk deliveries or stabilizing sick newborns (calls come from nurses and/or ER doctors – NOT from parents)

SUPPORT & RESOURCES:

  • APRN support is provided Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday mornings, especially when census is highest.
  • CRNA is available 24/7 for epidurals and urgent/emergent C-sections.
  • The nursery, labor & delivery, postpartum unit, and pediatrics are located conveniently on the same floor.

SCOPE OF PRACTICE:

  • Typical Census: 8-15 newborns per day / 0-2 pediatric patients per day.
  • 90% of inpatient duties involve managing newborns, including nursery coverage.
  • 10% of duties involve managing straightforward pediatric admissions such as basic ENT cases.
  • No complex subspecialty care or PICU-level cases.
  • Procedures Include: Circumcisions, emergency CPAP management, frenotomies, and excision of simple polydactyly. Rare emergency procedures such as intubation, needle decompression of pneumothorax, and UVC placement.

LEVEL OF CARE & TRANSFERS:

  • Providers will work in a Level 2 nursery and must attend deliveries as early as 32 weeks gestation.
  • High-risk deliveries or newborns needing advanced care, such as mechanical ventilation or neonatal surgery, will be transferred to McLeod (Level 3 NICU) or MUSC (Level 4 NICU).
  • McLeod is accessible by ground transport within 2 hours.
  • MUSC is reachable via helicopter within 45 minutes.


ADDITIONAL INFORMATION:

  • Approximately 2,000 deliveries annually, expected to grow due to the expansion of the Women’s Health department and transfers from Grand Strand Medical Center.
  • Cerner EMR.

The Community:

This beautiful city is an artsy enclave on the Coast with world-class kite festivals draw thousands in the summer. Local glass blowers create distinctive and colorful glass floats, then clandestine “float fairies” shrewdly hide them along the shoreline for beachcombers. In the midst of beautiful Oregon coastal forests, several nearby hikes are also a thing to behold. Drift Creek Falls features a surprising scene in the middle of the woods: a 100-foot high suspension bridge over a 75-foot waterfall with Drift Creek below. On the edge of the Pacific, the wide-open trails at Cascade Head lead to panoramic views of Lincoln City’s coast, as well as Devil’s Lake and Cape Foulweather further out. Devil’s Lake and Siletz Bay provide large swaths of sheltered, open water for fishing, water sports, and swimming… disregarding old folk tales about a sea monster in the lake, of course.

The local public school district serves about 5,500 students from Kindergarten through 12th grade in 11 regular schools and 3 public charter schools, with a total of approximately 600 employees. Higher education is just a short drive away - 1 hour to Salem and 2 hours to Portland. Other nearby cities include: Depoe Bay - 12 Miles, Pacific City - 22 Miles, Newport - 25 Miles, Tillamook - 43, Dallas - 48 Miles, and Corvallis - 75 Miles.

job.description:
Seeking BE/BC Family Medicine or MedPed Physician or Advanced Practice Provider to join rural health clinic in coastal OR town, an hour west of Salem, that has been providing care to the community for almost 50 years.

The Community:

This beautiful city is an artsy enclave on the Coast with world-class kite festivals draw thousands in the summer. Local glass blowers create distinctive and colorful glass floats, then clandestine “float fairies” shrewdly hide them along the shoreline for beachcombers. In the midst of beautiful Oregon coastal forests, several nearby hikes are also a thing to behold. Drift Creek Falls features a surprising scene in the middle of the woods: a 100-foot high suspension bridge over a 75-foot waterfall with Drift Creek below. On the edge of the Pacific, the wide-open trails at Cascade Head lead to panoramic views of Lincoln City’s coast, as well as Devil’s Lake and Cape Foulweather further out. Devil’s Lake and Siletz Bay provide large swaths of sheltered, open water for fishing, water sports, and swimming… disregarding old folk tales about a sea monster in the lake, of course.

The local public school district serves about 5,500 students from Kindergarten through 12th grade in 11 regular schools and 3 public charter schools, with a total of approximately 600 employees. Higher education is just a short drive away - 1 hour to Salem and 2 hours to Portland. Other nearby cities include: Depoe Bay - 12 Miles, Pacific City - 22 Miles, Newport - 25 Miles, Tillamook - 43, Dallas - 48 Miles, and Corvallis - 75 Miles.

job.description:

  • Outpatient role
  • 30 minute appointments for new, sick and well-child visits
  • All clinical hours - no show rate is high (25%) which leaves plenty of time for charting and research
  • No assigned panel - all physicians rotate to service patient/family best. If need mroe time than allotted, another provider with pick up the next appointment.
  • NO weekends, NO holidays
  • Triage handles 99% of calls, most months you will get 1 or less calls
  • Full time = 5 days per week, Monday-Friday

  • No inpatient or ER coverage
  • Team of 1 other Pediatrician and 1 NP
  • Nonprofit: We are a small nonprofit with a team of 12. We have two providers at full staffed. We have a volunteer Pediatrician who dedicates her Thursdays to care for our patients.
  • Safety-net: Private practices in our area are almost obsolete. 92% of our families have Medicaid (3% private insurance and 5% on a sliding scale fee). This means more complicated patients and longer visits to help the patient and family handle their barriers to success/access. Because of the care we provide, you cannot meet a normal quota and our providers see on average 20 patients a day.
  • Community: We are the only pediatric community clinic in our region. Patients/Families come from 12 countries and 53 zip codes for our service in just one year. Generation-after-generation come to our clinic for care. Other clinics in our space are FQHCs and serve birth to death with Family Practice docs. We specialize in children! An actively licensed Anesthesiology/Pain Management Physician is needed to join our team and help care for our current patients. Successful candidates will have a solid knowledge of pain management and be experienced in surgeries related to the treatment of pain. As an outpatient clinic, our Pain Management Physician will be responsible for performing surgery, recommending medication and working with patients to create treatment plans tailored to their specific pain needs.

  • Outpatient only position with emphasis on interventional pain medicine, neuromodulation, and functional recovery.
  • 15-30 patients seen per day with assistance of a nurse practitioner
  • Team of 4 pain anesthesiologist and 5 nurse practitioners
  • Each practice location integrates outpatient clinic, diagnostic laboratory, physical therapy, diagnostic imaging, urgent care and ambulatory surgery center.

  • No evening or weekend call
  • Providers rotates among the 6 centers, usually monthly.
  • Monitor patient reactions to surgery and anesthesia.
  • Administer pain medication to lessen the intensity of post-surgical pain.
  • Use appropriate methods of monitoring a patient's vital signs during surgery and recovery.
  • Review patient records to identify potential risks and complications before, during, and after surgery; able to identify the effects of anesthesia on various organs before, during, and after surgery.
  • Dispense medications that may be used during or after surgery;.
  • Serve as an expert in airway management including specialized techniques such as fiberoptic bronchoscopy, video laryngoscopy, and one lung ventilation
  • Use specialized equipment including, but not limited to specialized monitoring devices, laryngoscopes, bronchoscopes, ventilators, and ultrasounds
  • Evaluate for and perform anesthetics including monitored anesthesia care, general anesthesia, and/or regional anesthesia as is appropriate for the patient
  • Placement of invasive monitoring as is appropriate for the patient
  • Provide acute and chronic pain management

Compensation & Benefits:

  • Base salary with 50% of collections
  • 4 weeks PTO (20 working days)
  • Comprehensive benefits package
  • CME
  • Malpractice
  • No state income tax!

Area Highlights:

Coeur d’Alene, perched in a beautiful lakefront mountain setting, is becoming a favorite destination for retirees and many others fleeing other urban areas, especially on the Pacific coast. There is plenty to do and the summer climate is particularly pleasant and fresh. Downtown is clean and vibrant. Most residential and commercial areas spread into the relatively flat landscape to the north. Spokane to the west is close enough to provide amenities and services plus employment for those who need it. But there is plenty to do locally, with numerous recreation, entertainment and minor arts amenities. The local construction boom, tourism, and some light commercial activity round out a healthy economic climate.

Nearby Spokane, WA has a mild climate all 4 seasons, therefore has opportunities for year-round outdoor activities. For summer time, there is water skiing, camping, white water rafting or sitting by the lake. For winter, there are 5 snow skiing resorts within 2 hours of downtown. There are numerous great restaurants and a variety of cultural events that come to town each month. There are 3 major universities that serve our area, plus a great public and private school system.

For over 38 years the system has provided care to a service area population numbering about 35,000 people. Its has a dedicated, volunteer Board of Directors and a strong, supportive relationship with the Medical Center. It has received recognition as a Patient-Centered Medical Home (PCMH). PCMH is a comprehensive, coordinated team-based approach that enables patients to take an active role in their health status and decision making. This innovative model puts patients at the center of care as their primary care practitioner leads an interdisciplinary team of health care professionals to treat all aspects of the patient’s health. NCQA Patient-Centered Medical Home Recognition raises the bar in defining high-quality care by emphasizing access, health information technology, and coordinated care focused on patients.

The clinic strives to be the leading provider of exceptionally comprehensive, affordable, and universal care to its dialysis patients today in a very friendly atmosphere, where patients’ welfare is the top priority. Group currently includes 5 Nephrologists, located in the Atlanta, GA suburbs. Partnership track available.

  • New grads welcome.
  • Physician offices on premises.
  • Dietitian on staff.
  • Social Worker on staff.
  • Well-trained/Multilingual staff.
  • Lab on site.
  • Vacation: 4 weeks + 1 week for CME
  • Base Salary: $250,000
  • Bonus: 50% bonus after $650,000 in production
  • Current Call Schedule: 1:4

Clinic treats kidney diseases and disorders including the following:

  • Chronic Kidney Diseases Management
  • Diabetes Management
  • Hemodialysis (blood dialysis)
  • Peritoneal Dialysis (stomach Dialysis)
  • Electrolyte Imbalance
  • Management of High Blood Pressure (Hypertension)
  • Inflammation of Kidneys (Glomerulonephritis)
  • Kidney Failure (Renal Failure)
  • Kidney Transplant
  • Low Blood Count (Anemia)
  • Hematuria (Blood in urine)

job.title: Family Medicine opening in N. Central Minnesota
job.description:
We are seeking a Family Medicine Physician to join our growing primary care team in Park Rapids, MN! This high-volume practice provides a wonderful small-town feel and team-focused atmosphere for someone to truly settle into a warm and welcoming community. Entire provider team includes Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, Nurse Midwifery, Pediatrics, General Surgery and Behavioral Health with exceptional support staff and many outreach specialty services provided weekly/monthly.

  • Full-time, 1.0 FTE opportunity (36 patient contact hours; 32 patient contact hours if doing OB)
  • Hours: Monday-Friday between 8a-5p
  • Based in Park Rapids, MN with potential outreach to Menahga and Walker clinics
  • Outpatient practice (opportunity for inpatient and nursing home rounds, if desired.)
  • Procedures and OB services welcome but not required (130 deliveries per year); c-sections can be performed (only scheduled) but need collaborating provider to take care of baby; emergent c-sections are covered by general surgery.
  • Average Clinic Patients per day:15-20
  • Call Coverage: 1:10 via telephone
  • Onsite Services Include: Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, Nurse Midwifery, Pediatrics, Behavioral Health, General Surgery/Wound Care, Diabetes Education, Dietitian, Infusion Center, Path/Lab, Radiology/Imaging, Physical Therapy & Weight Loss/Bariatrics
  • Outreach Services Include: Audiology, Oncology, Dermatology, ENT, Cardiology, Nephrology, OB/GYN, Orthopedic Surgery, Podiatry & Rheumatology
  • NHSC and state loan repayment qualifying site

REQUIREMENTS

  • BC/BE Family Medicine


LOCATION

  • Centrally located in the heart of the lakes country
  • 3 hours north of Minneapolis/St. Paul
